paper_id: Yang et al. - 2015 - See Through Walls with COTS RFID System!
title: See Through Walls with COTS RFID System!
motivation: Emergency responders and civilians need low-cost through-wall tracking, but existing radar tech costs $80K and is restricted to military use.
problem_framing: Extract weak object reflections from backscatter signals while drowning out the stronger 'flash' reflections off walls, without hardware modifications.
key_insight: RFID backscatter vulnerability to ambient reflections is reframed as an opportunity—tags on outer wall become a virtual antenna array sensing interior objects.
method_signature: Subtract empty-room baseline to eliminate flash, divide by LOS signal to cancel device parameters, HMM/Viterbi for trajectory recovery.
evaluation_criteria: Median tracking error (cm), wall penetration depth (inches), gesture decoding accuracy (%), system cost (USD).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: System exceeds FCC power limits with 12dBi antenna; requires pre-learning empty room; tracks only one object; directional dependence limits deployment area.
